Robot Doctor Sensors & odometry

Odometry / Pinpoint position is wrong or drifts

Robot thinks it's somewhere it isn't. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Do you track position with dead wheels or a Pinpoint / OTOS (not just drive motor encoders)? Dead wheels are small unpowered omni wheels with encoders.
  • Pushing the robot forward by hand, does X go up (and pushing left, does Y go up)? Run your localization test and watch telemetry while you push.
  • If you spin in place a few times, do X and Y drift far from 0? Turn the robot several full circles in place and look at X/Y.
  • Are you using a goBILDA Pinpoint? The small odometry computer the dead wheels plug into.
  • Does heading slowly change while the robot sits perfectly still? Leave it alone for 30 seconds with telemetry up.
  • Do the dead wheels spring firmly onto the floor everywhere on the field? Push each pod up and let go, and watch it over tile seams.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Odometry pod direction is reversed

If a pod counts backward, position runs off the opposite way as soon as you move.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Run a localization test and push the robot by hand.
  2. Forward should make X go up, pushing left should make Y go up, and turning counter-clockwise should make heading go up.
  3. Reverse whichever pod is wrong (Pinpoint: setEncoderDirections).

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting · goBILDA · Pinpoint user guide (PDF) · Pedro Pathing · Pinpoint tuning

2 Pod offsets are wrong or swapped

Offsets tell the localizer where each pod sits from the robot's turning center. Wrong ones show up as drift when the robot turns.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Spin the robot in place several times. If X/Y wander far from 0, the offsets are off.
  2. Measure from the center of rotation and follow your library's sign convention exactly (Pinpoint: X offset is how far sideways the forward pod is, left positive; Y offset is how far forward the strafe pod is, forward positive).
  3. Make sure the forward and strafe pods are not swapped (Pinpoint: forward pod in the X port).
  4. Pedro Pathing's Pinpoint auto-tuner can measure offsets for you.

Sources: Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting · goBILDA · Pinpoint user guide (PDF) · Pedro Pathing · Pinpoint tuning

3 Pinpoint mounted or calibrated wrong

The Pinpoint must be mounted sticker side up, and its IMU calibrates at power-on. Moving the robot then gives a heading that drifts while sitting still.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Mount the Pinpoint flat, sticker side (with the ports) facing up.
  2. Keep the robot still when it powers on, or call recalibrateIMU() / resetPosAndIMU() while the robot is still at the start of your OpMode.
  3. If you run a flywheel, isolate the Pinpoint from vibration. It can cause slow drift.
Recalibrate while still
odo.resetPosAndIMU();   // robot must be completely still
sleep(300);

Sources: goBILDA · Pinpoint user guide (PDF) · Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

4 Dead wheel loses contact with the floor

Without enough spring force, a pod skips or lifts over seams and stops counting accurately.

How to fix it 20 min

  1. Push down on each pod. It should spring back firmly and always touch the tiles.
  2. Add spring or rubber band tension so the wheel stays planted, and make sure it moves freely up and down.
  3. Check the pod wheel spins freely and the encoder cable has slack for the pod to move.

Sources: GM0 · Dead wheels

5 Tracking with drive-motor encoders

Mecanum wheels slip, especially when accelerating hard, so drive encoders lose track over a match.

How to fix it varies

  1. Limit acceleration in autonomous so wheels do not slip.
  2. For accurate autos, add dead wheels or a Pinpoint / OTOS, and correct with AprilTags when you can see them.

Sources: GM0 · Dead wheels
